subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should OpenClaw solve issue #41484 as a narrow per-job/heartbeat elevated flag, or fold it into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The requested behavior changes the trust boundary for elevated host exec across persisted cron jobs, agent-created schedules, heartbeat files/config, and upgrade behavior, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
options.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

options.title: Implement Narrow Elevated Markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-modifier elevated approval state now, with explicit migration and tests for create, update, and execution-time checks.

options.title: Fail Closed For Internal Sources
options.body: Remove wildcard-style internal-source elevation for cron-event and heartbeat unless maintainers intentionally preserve a compatibility mode.

recommendation.title: Fold Into Scheduling Provenance
recommendation.body: Treat #41484 as the elevated-exec requirement for the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design while keeping heartbeat provenance in scope.

likelyOwner.reason: #96883 is the closest recent merged cron provenance/security-boundary work and touched the cron tool, Gateway cron server, and protocol schema paths this design would likely build on.
